title: About You
text: I’m a Boston University student exploring how data can help businesses make better decisions. Through coursework, I’m developing the technical foundation to turn complex information into clear, practical insights. I enjoy working through questions that connect numbers to real decisions: What is driving a change in performance? Which patterns deserve a closer look? How can an analysis help someone decide what to do next? ## What I’m learning My academic interests bring together business problem-solving and hands-on technical work. I’m building experience with: - Python and data analysis: organizing data, exploring patterns, and communicating findings. - SQL and Apache Spark: working with structured data and learning how to analyze larger datasets. - Cloud analytics: understanding how cloud tools support scalable data workflows. - Statistics and visualization: using evidence and clear charts to explain results. I value an approach that starts with a clear question, checks the quality of the data, and explains both the findings and their limitations. ## Where I’m headed My goal is to pursue a data analyst or business analyst role where I can combine technical skills with an understanding of business needs. I’m particularly interested in using analytics to improve operations, understand customer behavior, and measure performance. As I continue learning, I want to build a portfolio of projects that shows how I think: define the problem, explore the evidence, and turn the results into useful recommendations. ## Beyond the coursework I’m curious about emerging technology and enjoy learning through practical projects. This website is a place to share that progress, reflect on what I’ve learned, and connect with others interested in business and data.
